title: pk adopt source (program-kit.adoption.v1)
description: The one file a programme that ran before the kit exports so that `pk adopt <file>` moves it onto the kit, once. Every top-level key is required and no other is allowed. Paths are repository-relative, posix, and name files or directories committed at HEAD.

primary_branch.description: the kit's primary branch is fixed as main

legacy_phase_prefixes.description: phase IDs the register may use besides P<n>; milestone, step and task IDs follow (CX, CX-M01, CX-M01-S01, CX-M01-S01-T01)

phases.description: exactly the shape of program/register.yaml; `pk register validate` must pass on it

statuses.description: read for shape only in this kit version: a non-empty list is refused (statuses import arrives in KA-2)

path.description: the legacy rulings log, copied byte for byte to program/legacy/rulings.md; its blocks start at lines `## R<n> ...`

next.description: the first ruling number the kit issues: one past the legacy log's last ruling

followups.description: F-0001 to F-(next-1) must each be listed once, open or closed: the kit issues F-<next> next

adhoc.description: ad-hoc tasks in source order: the n-th becomes AH-<nnnn> and keeps legacy_id; done reads as closed and in_progress as progress

legacy_id.description: the task's name before adoption; unique, and not a register task ID

costs.description: the source rows as they are. at, task, role and model are required text, tokens, tool_calls and seconds whole numbers; agent defaults to "unknown" and resume to false; other keys are kept. A task that is a register ID is kept, a legacy ad-hoc name becomes its AH- ID, anything else is kept with legacy_task: true (a key the source must not carry)

path.description: the legacy hand-off, copied byte for byte to program/legacy/HANDOFF.md

now.description: the controller's one line: what it is doing

legacy_evidence_roots.description: directories committed at HEAD that hold the evidence from before adoption
